chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

key_terms.الرَّحِيلُ: Departure or leaving (specifically from this world)
key_terms.وَشِيكٌ: Imminent, close at hand, or near

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'Al-Rahil Washik' mean in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this concise saying from Nahj al-Balagha, Amīr al-mu’minīn (peace be upon him) uses the metaphor of 'departure' to emphasize the immediacy of death, urging believers to maintain spiritual readiness at all times. This aphorism reflects the Shia emphasis on *zuhd* (asceticism) and the constant awareness of the Hereafter (*mawt*) as a catalyst for righteous action. It serves as a poignant reminder that the transition from this transient world to the eternal realm is not distant but ever-present.
